questions.question: What powers a main-sequence star?
questions.reference_answer: Hydrogen fusion into helium in the core (proton-proton chain / CNO cycle).

questions.question: What is one astronomical unit and its value in kilometres?
questions.reference_answer: Defined as exactly 149,597,870,700 m, about 149.6 million km, roughly the Earth-Sun distance.

questions.question: How is distance in parsecs related to parallax?
questions.reference_answer: d(pc) = 1 / p(arcsec): the reciprocal of the parallax angle in arcseconds.

questions.question: What causes the seasons on Earth?
questions.reference_answer: The tilt of Earth's rotation axis (~23.4°) changes sunlight angle and day length; distance to the Sun is not the cause.

questions.question: Why does the Moon show nearly the same face to Earth?
questions.reference_answer: Tidal locking: its rotation period equals its orbital period (synchronous rotation); small libration lets us see a bit more than half.

questions.question: Why does a comet develop a tail near the Sun?
questions.reference_answer: Solar heating sublimates ice, releasing gas and dust; solar wind and radiation pressure push them away from the Sun.

questions.question: What does a transit light curve measure and what does depth encode?
questions.reference_answer: Dimming of a star as a planet crosses it; depth ≈ (Rp/Rs)², giving radius ratio, not mass.

questions.question: What is the radial-velocity method for finding planets?
questions.reference_answer: Measures periodic Doppler shifts in stellar spectra caused by the star's reflex motion; yields a minimum mass (m sin i).

questions.question: What is the event horizon of a black hole and what sets the Schwarzschild radius?
questions.reference_answer: Boundary beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape; r_s = 2GM/c², proportional to mass.

questions.question: What supports a white dwarf against gravitational collapse?
questions.reference_answer: Electron degeneracy pressure; the Chandrasekhar limit is ~1.4 solar masses.

questions.question: What is the cosmic microwave background?
questions.reference_answer: Relic radiation from recombination ~380,000 years after the Big Bang, now a ~2.725 K blackbody.

questions.question: What is the Hubble-Lemaître relation at low redshift?
questions.reference_answer: v = H0 d: recession velocity proportional to distance, with H0 in km/s/Mpc.

questions.question: What do the axes of a Hertzsprung-Russell diagram show, and why does extinction matter for a colour-magnitude diagram?
questions.reference_answer: Luminosity/absolute magnitude versus temperature/colour; dust dims and reddens stars, shifting them.

questions.question: What does specific impulse describe?
questions.reference_answer: Thrust per unit weight flow of propellant, expressed in seconds; higher Isp means more efficient propellant use.

questions.question: Since Pluto is the largest planet in the Solar System, how long does it take to orbit the Sun?
questions.reference_answer: Premise is false: Pluto is a dwarf planet and Jupiter is the largest planet. Pluto's orbital period is about 248 years.

questions.question: How did the Apollo 8 crew land on the Moon in 1968?
questions.reference_answer: Apollo 8 orbited the Moon (Dec 1968) but did not land; the first landing was Apollo 11 in July 1969.

questions.question: At what radius does the Sun's event horizon form?
questions.reference_answer: The Sun has no event horizon; it is not a black hole. Its hypothetical Schwarzschild radius would be ~2.95 km.

questions.question: Why does a transit light curve directly give a planet's mass?
questions.reference_answer: It does not; transits give the radius ratio and period. Mass needs radial velocity or transit timing variations.

questions.question: Explain why a Hohmann transfer minimizes the travel time between two circular orbits.
questions.reference_answer: It does not minimize time; under its assumptions it minimizes delta-v (fuel), and faster transfers cost more delta-v.

questions.question: Since COBE discovered the cosmic microwave background in 1990, what did it show?
questions.reference_answer: The CMB was discovered in 1964-65 by Penzias and Wilson; COBE (1989 launch, results from 1990) measured its blackbody spectrum and later detected anisotropies.

questions.question: Why is Venus the planet closest to the Sun?
questions.reference_answer: Mercury, not Venus, is closest to the Sun; Venus is second.

questions.question: Why is the far side of the Moon permanently dark?
questions.reference_answer: It is not dark; the far side receives sunlight as the Moon rotates. It is permanently hidden from Earth because of tidal locking.

questions.question: Is there life on Europa?
questions.reference_answer: Unknown: Europa has a subsurface ocean, but no evidence of life has been found.

questions.question: What is the value of the Hubble constant?
questions.reference_answer: About 67-68 km/s/Mpc from the CMB (Planck) and ~73 km/s/Mpc from local distance ladders; the Hubble tension is unresolved.

questions.question: What is dark matter made of?
questions.reference_answer: Unknown; inferred only from gravity. Candidates include WIMPs, axions, sterile neutrinos and primordial black holes; none is confirmed.

questions.question: When will the Sun become a red giant?
questions.reference_answer: In roughly 5 billion years, approximately; exact timing depends on stellar models.

questions.question: Can you give the exact reentry date of a satellite currently at 400 km altitude?
questions.reference_answer: No: reentry timing is uncertain because atmospheric density varies with solar activity and attitude/drag.

questions.question: Exactly how many galaxies are in the observable universe?
questions.reference_answer: Not known exactly; estimates range from ~10^11 to ~2×10^12 depending on faint-galaxy assumptions.
